summary: This resolution expresses the sense of the House that President Trump, Special Envoy Witkoff, and other federal officials must immediately transfer to the Treasury any payments received from the United Arab Emirates or other foreign states and divest from all business interests tied to foreign governments to comply with the Foreign Emoluments Clause.

scores.thoughts: The resolution addresses compliance with the Foreign Emoluments Clause, requiring officials to turn over foreign payments to the Treasury and divest business interests. It does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any government expenditures or budgets.
No provisions relate to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or changes in taxation for individuals or corporations.
The bill contains no references to healthcare systems, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
No content addresses firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The resolution does not discuss immigration policy, borders, visas, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions or language relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
While national security risks are mentioned in passing, the bill does not address military budgets, defense spending levels, or armed forces policy.
No engagement with environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation measures.
The text does not reference welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
No provisions concern schools, education funding, or school choice.
The resolution makes no reference to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No content addresses sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.

Mentions of semiconductor exports and AI investments appear only as factual background for alleged emoluments violations; the resolution itself does not set trade policy, tariffs, or globalization rules.
No discussion of deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions concern foreign aid appropriations or policy.
The resolution does not engage with voting access, election integrity, or electoral reforms.
References to cryptocurrency and AI technology are incidental to the emoluments issue and do not propose regulation, oversight, or privacy protections.
No content relates to worker protections, unions, or labor policy.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination law.
